seoTitle: How to Join a Channel in Slack (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: Browse and join public Slack channels using the workspace directory, filter by channel type, and see joined status before you commit.
intro: Staying connected to the right project rooms and department updates gets harder as a Slack workspace grows past a handful of channels. This guide covers where the full channel list actually lives in the current Slack layout, how to tell which ones you're already in, and how to filter down to just the channels you haven't joined yet so you're not scrolling past ones you're already a member of.

steps.heading: Start from your Channels list in the sidebar
steps.body: The left sidebar shows a Channels section listing every room you've already joined, with an "Add channels" link underneath it for anything new. This is your home base for daily use, but it only shows channels you're already in — it won't surface public rooms you haven't joined yet, which is why finding new ones means going somewhere else in the app. Below Channels you'll also see Direct messages and any installed Apps, all sharing the same sidebar real estate.

image.caption: The sidebar's Channels section, listing the rooms you've already joined with an Add channels link for finding more.

steps.heading: Open Directories and switch to the Channels tab
steps.body: Click Directories in the left sidebar, then select the Channels tab at the top — this is the actual full-workspace channel list, distinct from the short one in your sidebar. Each row shows the channel name, its member count, a short description, and whether you've already joined it. A banner at the top reminds you that channels are meant for organizing conversations by project, group, or topic, with a Create Channel button next to the search bar if none of the existing ones fit.

image.caption: The Directories panel's Channels tab — the real browsable list, showing member counts, descriptions, and Joined status per channel.

steps.heading: Filter the list down to channels you haven't joined
steps.body: The dropdown above the list defaults to "All channels," which mixes ones you're in with ones you're not. Switch it to "Other channels" to see only the rooms you haven't joined yet, or "My channels" to double back and confirm what you're already a member of. On a workspace with dozens of channels this filter does the job the old keyword search used to — it narrows the list fast without you having to read every description.

image.caption: The channel list filter dropdown, switching between All channels, My channels, and Other channels.

steps.heading: Check a channel's description before joining
steps.body: Each row in the directory carries a one-line description set by whoever created the channel — read it before joining, since names alone can be ambiguous on a busy workspace. A channel marked "Required" means it's mandatory for everyone in the workspace and you likely can't leave it even if you wanted to; anything without that tag is optional. If a channel's purpose still isn't clear from its description, open it directly to skim recent messages before committing.

steps.heading: Join the channel and confirm it in your sidebar
steps.body: Click a channel's row (or its Join button, on rooms you haven't joined) to add it to your account. It appears back in your sidebar's Channels list immediately, and in most workspaces you can scroll back through its full message history from before you joined, not just new activity going forward. If your sidebar starts feeling cluttered after joining several, drag channels into custom sections to group them by project or team instead of leaving everything in one flat list.

faq.question: Can I join a private channel the same way?
faq.answer: No, private channels don't appear in the public Directories list — you need an invite or request from an existing member to get into one.

faq.question: How do I leave a channel later?
faq.answer: Open the channel, click its name at the top, and choose Leave channel from the details menu — unless it's marked Required, in which case you may not be able to.

faq.question: Can I organize joined channels into custom sections?
faq.answer: Yes, drag any channel in your sidebar into a custom section, or create a new section from the Channels header's options menu.

faq.question: Will I see message history from before I joined?
faq.answer: Yes, in most workspaces new members can scroll back through a public channel's full history once they join.

faq.question: What's the difference between 'All channels' and 'Other channels' in the filter?
faq.answer: All channels shows everything in the workspace regardless of membership. Other channels filters that list down to only the ones you haven't joined yet.
